Definition: from G1537 and G59; to buy up, i.e. ransom; figuratively, to rescue from loss (improve opportunity):--redeem.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, exagorázō is the word for redeem. In Galatians 3:13, the text says "Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law." In Galatians 4:5, the text says "To redeem them that were under the law."
TheologicalSignificance: What exagorázō teaches me is that redemption is God buying back what was lost, at a cost He paid Himself. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
